precepts.text: Give diligence to make your calling and election sure, for the word must be gone over constantly.
precepts.point: The Most High was working with these brothers to make them mighty. When we go into the street it is not a physical war, but we are to stand against three hundred with the word. This is why we must study, and make our calling and election sure.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”. The word must be gone over constantly.

Eleazar the son of Dodo, “one of the three mighties”, stood with David where the Philistines gathered in a parcel of ground full of barley, and “the people fled from before the Philistines.” But “they set themselves in the midst of that parcel, and delivered it, and slew the Philistines; and the Lord saved them by a great deliverance.” The Most High was working with these brothers to make them mighty.

When we go into the street it is not a physical war, but we are to stand against three hundred with the word. This is why we must study, and make our calling and election sure.

points: All Israel gathered to David at Hebron, confessing they were his bone and flesh, and remembering that even when Saul was king David led Israel out and brought them in.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: The Most High had said to David, "Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be ruler over my people Israel." The phrase "my people Israel" is repeated, and the Bible does not change.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: The elders came to Hebron, David made a covenant with them before the Most High, and they anointed him king according to the word of the Most High by Samuel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, which is Jebus, and the Jebusites told him he would not come in. Nevertheless David took the castle of Zion, the city of David.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: David said whoever smote the Jebusites first would be chief and captain. Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first and became chief.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: David dwelt in the castle and built the city round about from Millo, Joab repaired the rest, and David grew greater and greater because the Most High of hosts was with him.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: These are the chief of David's mighty men who strengthened themselves with him to make him king according to the word of the Most High concerning Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: Jashobeam, chief of the captains, lifted his spear against three hundred slain by him at one time. Our forefathers did for real what fighting films only imitate.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: Eleazar the son of Dodo, one of the three mighties, stood with David at Pas-dammim where the Philistines gathered to battle in a parcel of ground full of barley.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: When the people fled, they set themselves in the midst of the parcel, delivered it, and slew the Philistines, and the Most High saved them by a great deliverance.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: Three of the thirty captains went down to the cave of Adullam while the Philistines were encamped in the valley of Rephaim and their garrison was in Bethlehem.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: David longed and said, "Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem, that is at the gate." A stronghold is a solid place to gather troops and plan, near enough to strike but not so close as to be found out.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: The three broke through the Philistine host, drew the water, and brought it to David, but he would not drink it and poured it out to the Most High, saying he would not drink the blood of men who had put their lives in jeopardy. That was the heart of David.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: Abishai the brother of Joab was chief of the second three, and lifted his spear against three hundred and slew them, gaining a name among the three.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: He was more honourable than the other two and was their captain, but he did not attain to the first three. There is order, structure, and rank, just as the Most High has angels and archangels.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a valiant man of many acts, slew two lionlike men of Moab, went down and slew a lion in a pit on a snowy day, and killed an Egyptian five cubits high.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: He plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, a spear like a weaver's beam, and slew him with his own spear.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: These acts gave Benaiah a name among the three mighties. He was honourable among the thirty but did not attain to the first three, and David set him over his guard.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 11: David Anointed and His Mighty Men

points: The roll of the valiant men of the armies follows, including Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem, and many more named men from across the tribes.

Among them is Uriah the Hittite, one of David's valiant men, the same one David later had killed. Men called by the land they lived in, such as the Hittite or one of Moab, were Israelites dwelling in those lands.
